points.quote: a document doesn't have a separate edgeless copy. Page mode and edgeless mode are two views of one Yjs block tree.
The other is `affine:surface`, which holds the whiteboard layer.

Shapes, brush strokes, connectors, text, mind maps and groups are not blocks. They are "surface elements" stored inside the single `affine:surface` block. The surface model defines `elements: Boxed(new Y.Map())`
Page mode renders the notes as a linear document. Edgeless mode renders the same note blocks as movable cards on the canvas
Several block types can sit directly under the surface... These are frames, edgeless text, and in some cases bookmarks and attachments. These blocks are stored as ordinary blocks.
Surface elements and the block-based edgeless items (notes, frames, edgeless text) use the same field.
`index` is a fractional-index string... Elements are sorted by it... It applies to blocks and elements alike
A group element (`GroupElementModel`) has a `children` Y.Map of `{childId: true}`... A frame block has `childElementIds`... they test containment by bounds.
